items.note: Search summary: ERJ population study found FEV1 rise >=12% and 200 mL in 17.3% of asthma and 18.4% of COPD participants, so not specific.

items.sentence: In NICE COPD guidance (NG115) a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7, with typical symptoms, confirms airflow obstruction; GOLD uses the same fixed ratio. ERS/ATS 2022 interpretive standards instead use the lower limit of normal (a z-score below -1.645), and many laboratories report it. ...
items.note: NICE: post-bronchodilator spirometry confirms COPD; NICE COPD register indicator and UK summaries use <0.7 (the NG115 PDF text itself was not returned verbatim). GOLD 2023: fixed ratio <0.7, acknowledges LLN debate. ERS/ATS 2022 summary: LLN 5th percentile, z -1.645.

items.sentence: In UK asthma guidance (BTS/NICE/SIGN NG245) an FEV1 rise of 12% or more and 200 mL or more after a bronchodilator supports asthma; ERS/ATS 2022 uses a rise of more than 10% of the predicted value. A similar response is also seen in some people with COPD, so it is read with the history and other tests. ...
items.note: NG245 algorithm/guideline summary: 12% and 200 mL; algorithm also accepts 10% of predicted. ERS/ATS 2022: >10% of predicted FEV1 or FVC.

items.sentence: People over 35 who smoke or used to, with symptoms such as breathlessness or persistent cough (case-finding for COPD in people with symptoms)
items.note: NG115: suspect COPD in people over 35 with a risk factor (generally smoking or a history of it) and one or more symptoms; summaries list exertional breathlessness, chronic cough, regular sputum, winter bronchitis, wheeze. The symptom list itself was not in the retrieved NICE text.

items.sentence: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7 -> Airflow obstruction; with typical symptoms this confirms COPD in UK guidance. Severity graded by FEV1 as % predicted
items.note: 'Poor reversibility' dropped: retrieved NICE text says routine reversibility testing is not necessary for diagnosis. 'Severity graded by FEV1' is unchanged original wording, not re-retrieved.
